<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (symbol, 43 pages)`, `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 43 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e073455929a60b67c48da3f91324261e57aaa26b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d6f479abddd9515db1df9e3cf4e3dc646e027124` — the merge of head `18b8b6fa5dd3d24e8879c3291e6c2bf4b95023ae` into base `e073455929a60b67c48da3f91324261e57aaa26b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d6f479abddd9515db1df9e3cf4e3dc646e027124 && git checkout d6f479abddd9515db1df9e3cf4e3dc646e027124
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e073455929a60b67c48da3f91324261e57aaa26b 18b8b6fa5dd3d24e8879c3291e6c2bf4b95023ae && git checkout -B drift-repro e073455929a60b67c48da3f91324261e57aaa26b && git merge --no-ff 18b8b6fa5dd3d24e8879c3291e6c2bf4b95023ae

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e073455929a60b67c48da3f91324261e57aaa26b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e073455929a60b67c48da3f91324261e57aaa26b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `18b8b6fa5dd3d24e8879c3291e6c2bf4b95023ae`
Local-runs: none
Scope: every path of the diff outside the prose face (`.changeset/25561-analytics-read-gate-fault-503.md`): `packages/services/service-analytics/src/read-admission.ts`, `field-read-admission.ts`, `api-exposure-door.ts`, the five `service-analytics/src/__tests__/` pins (`read-admission-gate`, `field-read-admission-gate`, `field-query-admission-gate`, `api-exposure-door`, `unexposed-definition-registration`), `packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes.ts` + `build-probes-widget-refusal-fix.test.ts`, `packages/rest/src/analytics-read-gate-fault-envelope.test.ts` + the files those hunks make a claim about, read at the head: `packages/core/src/security/authz-store-unavailable.ts` (the precedent), `packages/rest/src/analytics-routes.ts` (the dataset route's catch, arm ③a) and `packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts` (`declaredServerFaultAnswer`, `thrownCodeFields`), `packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts` (`errorResponseBase` and the `/analytics/query` route), `packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts` + `error-code-ledger.zod.ts` (`StandardErrorCode`, `HttpStatusErrorCodeMap` `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE: 503`), `packages/services/service-analytics/src/plugin.ts` (the `admitObjectRead`, `getReadableFields` and `getObjectDeclaration` bridges), `analytics-service.ts` (gate order, `hasDeclaredErrorEnvelope`, the hook docblocks), `service-analytics/src/index.ts` + `package.json` `exports`, `packages/client/src/index.ts`, and the `content/docs/**` pages that mention analytics refusals.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Fail-closed preserved at all three sites: right.** `assertObjectsReadable` (`read-admission.ts`), `assertNamedFieldsReadable` (`field-read-admission.ts`) and `declarationOf` (`api-exposure-door.ts`) each keep the `try` scope they had on `main`. The `try` wraps only the provider call(s). Each catch still logs the cause at `error` (or `warn`) and still throws; only the thrown constructor changes. The verdict throws (`readAdmissionDeniedError`, `fieldReadDeniedError`, `fieldReadUnjudgeableError`, `internalFieldError`, `unexposedDefinitionError`) sit outside those `try` blocks, so a real denial cannot be caught and re-spelled as a fault. Nothing that was refused is admitted. `declarationOf` also feeds the internal-field gate (`assertNoInternalFieldsQueried`), so that read now also answers 503 on a throw. That is consistent with the card, and the exposure gate runs ahead of it on the same objects. The registration face (`assertDefinitionExposed`, `continue` on a throw) and the label face (`servesLabelTarget`, `return false`) have their own catches and are untouched.
- **Real denials byte-unchanged: right.** The diff touches only the docblocks of `readAdmissionDeniedError`, `fieldReadDeniedError` and `fieldReadUnjudgeableError`. Their bodies, messages, `code`, `status` and `object`/`fields`/`member` keys are not in a hunk. The exposure 404/405 constructors are not in a hunk. The verdict twins are pinned: the `!admitted` and hidden-field 403 pins stay unedited in the analytics suites, and the new rest seam asserts 403/403/404 beside each fault row through the real route.
- **The 503 envelope names only the object: right.** `readAdmissionUnresolvedError` throws `{ code: 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE', status: 503, object }`. Its message is the object name plus a fixed sentence: no gate, layer, grant, cause or existence fact. One constructor serves all three sites, so the message does not reveal which gate failed. The pins assert the message names the object and does not contain the cause (`exploded`, `reader unavailable`). This follows the shape of `authz-store-unavailable.ts`: the existing ADR-0112 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` code, which `HttpStatusErrorCodeMap` maps to 503. No code and no envelope key is added. The error is deliberately not marked `refusal: true`, so the prose stays the operator's.
- **Wire answer, dataset door (`POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query`): right, pinned.** A 503 skips the route's 4xx classification arm and reaches ③a `declaredServerFaultAnswer`. That arm relays `declaredHttpStatus` (503), gives `error: INTERNAL_ERROR_MESSAGE` (no `refusal` flag), and adds `code` through `thrownCodeFields`. `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` at 503 is consistent, so it is not demoted. The answer is `503 {"code":"SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE","error":"Internal server error"}`, not `500 ANALYTICS_QUERY_FAILED`. `logError` runs before the relay, so the operator line is kept. `hasDeclaredErrorEnvelope` in `analytics-service.ts` keeps the missing-source heuristics away from it. `analytics-read-gate-fault-envelope.test.ts` pins producer plus route for all three gates with a real `AnalyticsService` (Test Core green on this head). No `packages/rest` source change was needed, and none was made.
- **Wire answer, cube door (`POST /api/v1/analytics/query`): right, read, not pinned by this PR.** The route catches into `errorResponse`, and from there `errorResponseBase`, which takes `httpStatus` from `err.status` (503) and the code from `resolveThrownHttpError`. Because `serverFaultProvenance` is `'declared'`, the message is withheld. This is the same generic relay the existing `analytics-query-read-scope-withhold.test.ts` pins for a declared 500. The dev names the missing runtime pin as a deviation (outside the file surface). Not blocking.
- **Removed per-file constructors were not exported: right.** On `main`, `fieldReadUnresolvedError` and `exposureUnresolvedError` were bare `function` declarations (the `-` lines carry no `export`). `git grep` on `main` finds no reference outside their own files, tests included. The new `readAdmissionUnresolvedError` is a module `export` that only the two sibling modules import. `src/index.ts` does not re-export it, and the package's `exports` map has only `.`, so the published surface does not grow. No import cycle is added: `read-admission.ts` imports only types from `@objectstack/spec`.
- **Consumer `build-probes.ts`: right.** `readAdmissionRefusal` still keys only on `PERMISSION_DENIED`. The new `serviceUnavailableRefusal` is reached only when the error is not that refusal, and it keys on `code` (never the message). It changes only the `fix` text. The finding's `code`, `severity` and `message` are unchanged, and the function is not exported. Non-blocking observation: it matches any `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` from `queryDataset`, not only the analytics gates. The case that does reach it, `@objectstack/core`'s authz-store outage, fits the text, and any other 503 still gets a server-side remedy, which is better than "Fix the dataset definition…".
- **Other consumers of these refusals: no stale branch.** `packages/client/src/index.ts` does not branch on `PERMISSION_DENIED` or 403 for analytics. The `content/docs/**` analytics mentions make no fault-is-403 claim. The 403 sentences in `service-analytics/CHANGELOG.md` are release-owned history, which the changeset supersedes.
- **Side effect, named and right:** before this change, a core `AuthzStoreUnavailable` (503) thrown from inside the object-level provider was caught by `assertObjectsReadable` and re-spelled as 403. It now surfaces as 503, which agrees with the core ruling instead of masking it.
- **Gates:** 41 check-runs on the head. Every conclusion is `success` or `skipped`; the skipped runs are opt-in or matrix-placeholder jobs. Test Core 1–6, all Type Check and Lint families, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard and Dogfood Regression Gate are all `success`. None failed or is pending.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/service-analytics` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` is right. Both publish changed runtime behavior. `@objectstack/rest` gains only a test, so it publishes nothing and needs no entry.
- `Clause-②: no` is right. The test is whether the card widens the accept set or grows the public surface. It does neither: every request that was refused is still refused, every request that was served is still served, and no export is added. It is not `(narrowing)` either, because nothing that was served is now refused.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no authorable key, value, type or default moves. Under AGENTS.md's Post-Task Checklist step 3, a non-protocol change ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition. The changeset does that: a **BREAKING** banner with Before / Now / Fix (the consumer-side migration: treat `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` as a server fault and retry), and exactly one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker in the changeset body, beside both declaration lines. The PR body carries both lines at line start.
- The `!` in the PR title (`fix(service-analytics)!:`) matches a wire change on a fault path. The changeset's sentences match the diff, including "the cube query door relays the status the same way", which the read of `errorResponseBase` confirms.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions[0] (the plugin bridge's UNUSABLE branch still answers 403): leaving it out of THIS PR is right.** The card names three sites, and `plugin.ts` is outside the claimed file surface (the diff does not touch it). That branch is a `return false` verdict pinned at 403 by `admission-bridge-resolution.test.ts` (also untouched). On the in-repo kernels it is also the #22235 maintainer ruling's declared refusal for a deployment with no security service. Moving it would edit a ruled answer, so it needs the maintainer, and the seat has escalated it. This PR does not disturb that ruling. `callCtx` runs the object-level gate before the field-level gate, so a deployment with no security service is still refused by the object bridge's 403 before the field bridge, which now throws to 503, is reached. The UNUSABLE answer is byte-unchanged here. The PR body's acceptance note states that leftover asymmetry plainly.
- **Deviation: one `packages/rest` test, no rest source:** right. It pins the seam the card asks for, and it declares `OS_REST_LOG`, so `check-rest-log-spy-declared` is green.
- **Deviation: the two per-file constructors were folded into one shared one:** right. They were not exported (①), and one constructor is what keeps the no-oracle rule.
- **Deviation: cube door read but not pinned:** accepted (①). A runtime pin of the 503 through `/analytics/query` is a reasonable follow-up, not a blocker.
- **Deviations: PR-body footer and line order:** prose-face concerns for the lane seat, not a contract question here.
- **out_of_scope_findings[0]:** the same bridge as the open question, so it is answered by the escalation above.
- **Author:** the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay write), so no extra author note applies.

Reviewed-by: `session_01CxBKycaiUpA1yGx1XyoGqX`

**VERDICT: PASS**
